description.cancellation_policy:
Abuse of the permit system (multiple permits, false information, etc.) can result in cancellation of your permit and potential for you to be added to a restricted list.

Cancellation Policy: The permit holder may cancel their permit at any point prior to permit issuance/printing – no refunds are provided on cancellation of a permit reservation. Quota from cancelled permits will be immediately released and available to the public upon cancellation. 

Change Policy: Once created, the permit holder may modify their group size or itinerary locations prior to permit issuance/printing. If the group size is increased (quota permitting), the permit holder will be required to pay the additional $2 per person, per night recreation fee. If group size is reduced at any point, no refund is provided. The permit holder may not modify their permit start date; if the permit holder would like to change their start date, they will be required to cancel their existing reservation and book a new reservation.

description.description:
Everglades National Park protects an unparalleled landscape that provides important habitat for numerous rare and endangered species like the manatee, American crocodile, and the elusive Florida panther. The Marjory Stoneman Douglas Wilderness Area within Everglades National Park is the largest subtropical Wilderness in the United States. An Everglades Backcountry Wilderness permit allows overnight camping in the backcountry wilderness at chickee (elevated platform), ground and beach campsites.  

Visit the park's Wilderness Trip Planner before booking your permit.
description.discounts: There are currently no discounts available for permits.
description.driving_directions:
Everglades City and Chokoloskee, FL: Turn on to State Road 29, heading south. Designated launch sites are located in the Everglades City and Chokoloskee area.

Guy Bradley Visitor Center (Flamingo): 1 Flamingo Lodge Hwy, Homestead, FL 33034. Turn onto Palm Drive (State Road 9336/SW 344th St.) in Florida City heading west and follow the signs to the park. Expect to drive about an hour before arriving at Flamingo.

description.fee_policy:
Permit Reservation Fee: There is a $21 non-refundable permit reservation fee.

Recreation Fee: A $2 per person, per night recreation fee is required for the length of a reservation.

Entrance Fee: Everglades charges an entrance fee which you may pay upon arrival or purchase in advance. The park also honors valid annual or lifetime America the Beautiful-the National Parks and Federal Recreational Lands Passes (e.g. Senior, Military, 4th Grade, etc.) also known as interagency passes. For more information visit the park's Fees & Passes web page.
description.need_to_know_email:
• THIS CONFIRMATION EMAIL SERVES AS YOUR PERMIT. You are NOT required to pick up a physical permit, however, you are required to carry a physical copy or a screenshot of your final itinerary.

  • All paddlers and boaters must pay the entrance fee (separate from permit fees). Pay upon arrival or in advance. The park also honors valid annual & lifetime passes (e.g. Senior, Military, 4th Grade, etc.).

  • Powerboat operators must have a completion certificate from the Everglades Boater Education course. 

  • File a trip plan with a friend/relative before leaving. S/he is responsible to notify park dispatch at 305-242-7740 (non-emergency line) or 305-247-7272 (emergency line) if you don't return on schedule.

  • Stay at the site you selected on the specified date. 

  • Fires are allowed at beach sites only, below the high-tide line. Use down & dead wood only (no cutting of standing dead trees). Remove all traces of fires before leaving. Gas stoves/grills are allowed at ground or chickee sites, but fires and wood, charcoal, or coal fueled stoves/grills are prohibited.

  • Fresh water is not available anywhere along the coastal portions of the wilderness. You must bring all of your drinking & cooking water (minimum 1 gallon per person per day). 

  • Trash must be packed out. Do not bury, burn, or dispose of it in toilets. Dumping trash at sea is prohibited. 

  • Tides can heavily influence the time and difficulty to paddle to sites and to navigate shallow waters in a powerboat. Always check tide prediction tables. 

  • Pets are not permitted anywhere in the wilderness. 

  • Do not feed or harass any wildlife. Removal of any shell, animal, plant, or artifact is prohibited.

  • Use toilets where provided. Where not provided, pack out human waste or bury it at least 6” deep, and urinate directly into the water. Pack out toilet paper. Do not throw trash or wipes in toilets. 

  • Bring a nautical chart and compass with you. See NOAA's website for more information regarding nautical charts.

  • QUESTIONS? Call (239) 695-2945 or (786) 758-0635.

  • Water. Fresh water is not available along the coastal portions of the wilderness. Bring all drinking/cooking water (minimum: 1 gallon per person per day).

  • Pets. Pets are prohibited anywhere in the wilderness (including campsites or beaches). 

  • Wildlife. Do not feed or harass wildlife. Store food & water in hard containers or secure on a boat (not in tents). Removal of any shell, animal, plant, or artifact is prohibited.

description.need_to_know_permit:
BEFORE YOU RESERVE YOUR PERMIT:

  • Safely exploring the wilderness by water requires careful preparation and planning. Visit the Everglades Wilderness Trip Planner or if you require assistance planning your trip, call or stop by the Flamingo Visitor Center or call 786-758-0635 before booking your permit.

  • Permits are required for all overnight camping in the wilderness (except when sleeping aboard boats). If you need frontcountry (tent/RV) camping, you may reserve Flamingo and Long Pine campgrounds through Flamingo Adventures (an authorized park concessioner).

Everglades National Park designates campsites to prevent resource damage and to improve visitor experience. There are currently three types of campsites within the Marjory Stoneman Douglas Wilderness.   

  • Chickee Sites: Elevated platforms with roofs that give campers a unique experience of camping above the water's surface. Chickee platforms are 10 ft x 12 ft and are built to hold a maximum of 6 people or 1 group per platform. A group's tents must fit on one reserved platform. A portable toilet is provided at each chickee. Campfires, as well as wood, charcoal, and coal-fueled grills and stoves are not permitted. Use gas grills or stoves for cooking.   

  • Ground Sites. Along interior bays and rivers, typically on mounds of earth a few feet above the surrounding mangroves. Ground sites can accommodate larger groups and can hold multiple parties. Campfires, as well as wood, charcoal, and coal-fueled grills and stoves are not permitted. Use gas grills or stoves for cooking.

  • Beach Sites. Beach sites are located on the coast and provide opportunities for camping on the sand along the shoreline. Coastal breeze during ideal conditions makes insects scarce at times. Beach sites are the only type of campsite in the Wilderness where campfires are allowed, but fires must be built below high-tide line.

OTHER THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE YOU BOOK YOUR RESERVATION:

  • One permit can include multiple nights. A reservation may have multiple consecutive nights for a single $21 non-refundable permit reservation fee. Make sure to select all consecutive nights and campsites before proceeding to payment.

  • Bring a nautical chart and compass with you. See NOAA's website for more information regarding nautical charts.

  • Permit. A permit (digital or physical copy) with dates & campsites is required to camp in the wilderness area. 

  • Entrance Fee. All paddlers and boat operators must pay the Everglades entrance fee (separate from permit fees). Pay upon arrival or in advance. The park also honors valid annual & lifetime passes (e.g. Senior, Military, 4th Grade, etc.).

  • Safety course. A completion certificate from the Everglades Boater Education course is required for powerboat operators. 

  • Fires allowed at beach sites only. The park allows fires below the high-tide line. Use down & dead wood only (no cutting of standing dead trees). Remove all traces of fires before leaving. No fires at ground sites or chickees (we allow gas stoves or gas grills). 

  • Trash. Pack out all trash. Do not bury, burn, or dispose of it in toilets. Dumping trash at sea is illegal. 

  • Human Waste. Use toilets where provided. Where not provided, pack it out or bury it at least 6” deep. At beach and coastal ground campsites, urinate directly in the water. Pack out toilet paper with trash. Do not throw trash or wipes in toilets. 

  • Food. Remove all food particles from dishes before washing. Do not dump food scraps into the water; pack them out with trash. Wash dishes (and yourself) away from waterways and sprinkle the gray water over the ground to soak in.

  • You must bring all drinking and cooking water, a minimum of one gallon per person per day. Fresh water is not available anywhere along the coastal portions of the wilderness. 

  • Weather. Be prepared for intense sun, rain, strong winds, thunderstorms, lightning, and cold. Check the Weather forecast before departing. Carry a weather radio if possible. 

  • Tides. Tides can influence the time and difficulty to paddle to sites and to navigate shallow waters in a powerboat. Always check tide predictions for your trip.

  • Selected Site. You must stay at the site listed on this permit unless safety factors require otherwise. 

  • Noise. Be considerate of others when in close proximity. Generators and bug sprayers prohibited. 

  • Pets are not permitted anywhere in wilderness. This includes campsites & beaches. 

  • Fishing. Visit our fishing page for regulations.

  • Mosquitoes and no-see ums can be aggressive. Bring insect repellent, bug jackets, and/or long pants & sleeves.

  • Do not feed or harass any wildlife. Raccoons will do nearly anything to get food and water. Store both in hard-sided containers or secured aboard a boat (NOT in tents). 

  • Manchineel (Hippomane mancinella). This native, endangered, tree with shiny heart-shaped leaves is toxic. Contact causes severe burning.

  • Plants, animals, seashells, and artifacts are protected in the park. Removal prohibited.

  • Paddlers. When encountering motorboats in a narrow pass, as boat approaches, pull as far to the side as possible. Point the bow of your canoe or kayak into the boat’s wake.

  • Possession of firearms in the park is in accordance with federal, state, and local regulations. Discharge of a firearm prohibited.

  • Generators, chain saws, and other portable motors are prohibited.

  • Closed Areas. All keys in Florida Bay are closed to landing, except Bradley Key (open sunrise to sunset), and designated campsites. In Florida Bay, the mainland from Terrapin Point to U.S. 1 is closed to landing.

  • Vessels must meet Coast Guard safety regulations. Airboats and personal watercraft (jet skis) prohibited.
description.no_show_policy: No Show Policy: In the event a permit holder does not show up to their reserved site, their paid reservation is still held until the reservation expires or they enact a cancellation.
description.quota_details: 90-day rolling window for advance wilderness permit reservations. Quotas exist for each wilderness campsite for number of groups and number of people per site. Neither quota can be exceeded.
description.season_information:
This permit allows the permitted user and group to camp overnight at designated campsites within the Marjory Stoneman Douglas Wilderness. Book reservations online, year-round. Reservations open daily at 10:00 a.m. ET, 90-days before trip start date on a rolling basis. Making separate reservations for each night is not necessary. One permit/reservation per trip.

Your reservation confirmation email will serve as your permit. You are NOT required to pick up a physical permit in person, but you are required to carry a physical copy or screenshot of your final itinerary.

467531401.description:
Ground Site. Located on marl prairie, along a canal section of Alligator Creek, about 100 feet from Garfield Bight. Campers at this remote and rarely visited site will likely be gloriously alone, except for the crocodilians who often sun themselves at the landing. Mosquitoes can be abundant all year round.

Access - Accessible at all tides via the West Lake Canoe Trail (motors prohibited past West Lake). Florida Bay access limited: Garfield Bight is too shallow during strong North wind or low tide. Motors are allowed on the Florida Bay route. Foot trails are overgrown and not recommended. Ask for a map of Flamingo Area Canoe Trails if traveling on the West lake Canoe Trail. Obtain local knowledge from rangers for Florida Bay Route.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. Portable toilet is recommended. All plants, animals and artifacts in the park are protected. Absolutely no ground fires allowed! Pack out all trash.

Located:

  • 8.5 miles from West Lake Trailhead
  • 2.5 miles from Shark Point
  • 10.5 miles from Flamingo Marina

467531401.name: Alligator Creek (Ground Sites)

467531402.description:
Ground Site. Unique vegetation including bananas, limes, papayas, and wild sugarcane can be found on this old Indian mound which was occupied by the Seminole Indians in the early 1900s. There are flat, grassy sites shaded by the surrounding tropical hardwood trees.

Access - Accessible to canoes and powerboats with shallow draft and low clearance. Leave the Wilderness Waterway at marker #9 and travel 3.8 miles east through Tarpon Bay past the “No Wake” sign at the entrance to Avocado Creek. Continue up the creek to the campsite.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. Use camp stove. Dock, vault toilet, and picnic table are available. All plants, animals and artifacts in the park are protected. Pack out all trash. Warning signs advise against eating bass caught in this area due to high mercury content. 

Located:

  • 9.5 miles from Harney River Chickee
  • 8.5 miles from Shark River Chickee
  • 13.5 miles from Oyster Bay Chickee

467531402.name: Canepatch (Ground Sites)

467531403.description:
Beach Site. This campsite is a sand/marl beach, backed by mangroves and coastal prairie. Mosquitoes and sandflies may be a problem year round, especially if wind is out of the north.   

Access - Accessible by foot, powerboat, canoe or kayak. Site is located between Slagle and House Ditches on the southern coast. It can be reached by foot on Flamingo’s Coastal Prairie Trail, or by boat via Florida Bay. Low tide exposes mud flats, making it inaccessible by powerboat.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. Coastal Prairie Trail in summer is wet and muddy, six inches of water not uncommon. At low tides, this site is inaccessible to powerboats. Ground fires permitted below the high tide line. Use dead/down wood only. All plants, animals and artifacts in the park are protected. Pack out all trash, including toilet paper, and bury human waste 6” deep.   

Located:

  • 7.0 miles from Flamingo Marina
  • 5.0 miles from Carl Ross Key through Rocky Channel 
  • 3.0 miles from East Cape Sable
  • 7.5 miles from Middle Cape Sable

467531403.name: Clubhouse Beach (Beach Sites)

467531404.description:
Beach Site. This campsite is a sand/marl beach, backed by mangroves and buttonwoods. Mosquitoes and sandflies may be a problem year round, especially if wind is out of the north. The site affords a lovely view of northern Florida Bay. Many trekkers use this site as a final stopover in order to get an early return to Flamingo the next day.

Access - Accessible by powerboat, canoe or kayak, if consideration is given to the tide state. Low tide exposes mud flats, making it almost inaccessible. Site is located east of Slagle Ditch on the southern coast. It can be reached by boat from Florida Bay.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. Beach fires permitted below the high tide line. Use dead/down wood only. All plants, animals and artifacts in the park are protected, including seashells. Pack out all trash, including toilet paper, and bury human waste 6” deep.  

Located:

  • 4.0 miles from Flamingo Marina
  • 3.0 miles from Clubhouse Beach
  • 6.0 miles from East Cape Sable

467531404.name: East Clubhouse Beach (Beach Sites)

467531405.description:
Ground Site. Site is on a sand ridge on north side of Graveyard Creek, with large, flat, shady areas. Allow for strong 4 to 5 foot tidal fluctuations when securing boat.  

Access - Access for canoes and powerboats is limited due to exposed mud flats at the mouth of Graveyard Creek at low tide. Another route with deeper water starts southeast of the campsite and winds back to Graveyard Creek. Use a chart and obtain local knowledge of the area.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas.

No ground fires!    

Located:

  • 9 miles from Highland Beach

  • 6 miles from Harney River Chickee

  • 8 miles from Shark River Chickee

  • 10 miles from Oyster Bay

  • 11 miles from Northwest Cape Sable Be aware of the poisonous Manchineel trees at this site. Contact with or burning of any part of this plant may cause severe eye irritation, skin reactions/burns and temporary blindness. Manchineel has yellow-green leaves with a distinct mid-vein and slightly serrated edges. Eating fruit may be fatal.

467531405.name: Graveyard Creek (Ground Sites)

467531406.description:
Ground Site. The campsite is located on a small patch of slightly elevated ground. It is shaded by buttonwoods and surrounded by mangroves. Soil compaction at the site makes it very muddy after a rainstorm. The thick vegetation and shade can lead to high mosquito levels, especially in summer. 

Access - Accessible by paddlers from the Hell’s Bay Trail. Motors are prohibited from the Hells Bay Trail Head to Lard Can. The trail winds through mangroves and is protected from the wind for most of the way. White numbered PVC poles mark the route.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. No ground fires allowed. Portable stove or grill only. Vault toilet. Ask about trail conditions when getting a permit: occasionally markers are reported missing, and water levels drop during the dry season.  

Located:

  • 3.0 miles from Hells Bay Trailhead
  • 1.0 miles from Pearl Bay Chickee
  • 3.0 miles from Hells Bay Chickee
  • 5.5 miles from Lane Bay Chickee

467531406.name: Lard Can (Ground Sites)

467531407.description:
This chickee is located near Wilderness Waterway marker #12, just off the Harney River. In the evenings, watch for the flocks of ibises that fly up the Harney past the chickee on the way to their night’s roosting place. Wading birds prowl the mud flats at low tide.

Access - Accessible to canoes, kayaks, and powerboats at all tides from the Gulf of Mexico through the Harney River. For Wilderness Waterway followers in paddle craft, the site can be accessed by way of the “Nightmare” at marker #12 (high tide only).

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. There is a three foot tide differential and swift current. Cross mooring of vessels is necessary due to the tide differential. Pack out all trash.  

Located:

  • 8.5 miles from Broad River via the “Nightmare”
  • 9.5 miles from Canepatch
  • 10 miles from Shark River Chickee
  • 6 miles from Graveyard Creek

467531407.name: Harney River Chickee

467531408.description:
This site is so named because the bay was “hell to get to and hell to get out of!” This applies whether approaching from the Main Park Road via the twisty Hells Bay Canoe Trail, or from Whitewater Bay via the unmarked East River route. The chickee sits in the middle of the bay in front of a mangrove island. Alligators may be in the area. Do not allow food scraps to fall into the water near any chickee.

Access - Accessible by boat, canoe, and kayak at all tides via the East River from Whitewater Bay. Accessible via Hell’s Bay Canoe Trail (starts off park road), by canoe or kayak only. The site is located at the end of Hell’s Bay Trail near marker #178.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. East River route is not marked; a nautical chart is necessary to find the way through Whitewater Bay to the river mouth and to negotiate the tangle of creeks that comprise the river. The average water depth is 3 feet. This is a manatee Habitat. Be cautious! Do not hammer nails or stakes into chickees. Vault toilet. Portable stove only.  

Located:

  • 6.0 miles from Hells Bay Trailhead
  • 2.0 miles from Pearl Bay Chickee
  • 3.0 miles from Lard Can campsite
  • 2.5 miles from Lane Bay Chickee

467531408.name: Hell’s Bay Chickee

467531409.description:
Double Chickee. This site is located on an alternate route from the Wilderness Waterway on the east bank of the mouth of Joe River. The chickee sits in a small but beautiful cove. At night, listen for dolphins who puff their way past your home to fish in the creek behind the chickee. Tall trees block all but southwesterly breezes, so be prepared for tiny winged visitors.

Access - Accessible at all tides by powerboat, canoe, and kayak. From the Wilderness Waterway, travel southwest from marker #2 through Oyster Bay. Traveling through Joe River between Oyster Bay and Flamingo affords some protection from gusty winds and rough water common on Whitewater Bay, although Joe Bay can get quite rough on windy days.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. This is a manatee Habitat. Be cautious! Do not hammer nails or stakes into chickees. Portable stove or grill only.  

Located:

  • 9.0 miles from Shark River Chickee
  • 4.0 miles from Oyster Bay Chickee
  • 6.5 miles from South Joe River Chickee
  • 8.0 miles from Watson River Chickee

467531409.name: Joe River Chickee

467531410.description:
This site gets plenty of sun and breeze from the south, but is well protected from chilly northwest winds. Poisonwood and poison ivy are plentiful in the hardwood hammock against which the chickee is nestled. The view of Lane Bay is delightful.

Accessible by canoe, and kayak at all tides by taking the Hell’s Bay Trail and continuing north to Lane Bay. An alternate route suitable for powerboats exists through Whitewater Bay and Lane River. The average water depth is 3 feet.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. The site can be difficult to get to. A nautical chart is necessary to find the way. This is a manatee Habitat. Be cautious! Do not hammer nails or stakes into chickees. Vault toilet. Portable stove or grill only.  

Located:

  • 5.5 miles from Roberts River Chickee
  • 2.5 miles from Hells Bay Chickee
  • 4.5 miles from Pearl Bay Chickee
  • 8.5 miles from Hells Bay Trailhead

467531410.name: Lane Bay Chickee

467531411.description:
This campsite is located on the edge of a small mangrove island and is exposed to breezes from all but the west side. It fronts a beautiful bay. Osprey are seen fishing here during the day, as white pelicans wheel overhead.

Access - Accessible by boat, canoe, and kayak at all tides. This site is less used because it is off the beaten path. It is located on an unnamed river which parallels the North River. It is accessible by traveling upriver from Whitewater Bay, or by navigating through a series of interconnecting creeks from Roberts River Chickee.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. This is a manatee habitat. Be cautious! Do not hammer nails or stakes into chickees. Vault toilet. Portable stove or grill only. All plants, animals and artifacts in the park are protected. Pack out all trash.

Located:

  • 3.0 miles from Watson River Chickee
  • 5.5 miles from Coast Guard Marker #30
  • 3.0 miles from Roberts River Chickee
  • 8.0 miles from Hells Bay Chickee

467531411.name: North River Chickee

467531412.description:
This campsite is located in a protected cove relatively free from harsh weather. While the proximity of the cove shorelines can bring bugs, it makes for great wildlife viewing. Dolphins fish the waters alongside the nearby islands. At low tide, raccoons can be seen digging shellfish along the mud banks across the creek. The site gets its name from the many potentially dangerous oyster bars located nearby. 

Access - Accessible by boat, canoe, and kayak at all tides. It is one mile southwest of WW marker #2 in northern Oyster Bay. The site is popular with power boaters and paddlers alike. The chickee is situated at the intersection of the Wilderness Waterway and several Flamingo-to-Flamingo loop routes.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. Local knowledge will help navigate the oyster bars. This is a manatee habitat. Be cautious! Do not hammer nails or stakes into chickees. Vault toilet. Portable stove or grill only. All plants, animals and artifacts in the park are protected. Pack out all trash.

Located:

  • 10.0 miles from Graveyard Creek
  • 5.0 miles from Shark River Chickee
  • 4.0 miles from Joe River Chickee
  • 10.5 miles from South Joe River Chickee

467531412.name: Oyster Bay Chickee

467531413.description:
Accessible Site. This is the only chickee designed to accommodate campers with a disability or otherwise limited physical mobility. The platforms have railings on several sides, and there is a large chemical toilet. One of the platforms has steps leading down to the water to facilitate access. The chickee sits in the bay, away from the surrounding mangroves, and is open at all sides, so mosquitoes usually are not a problem. On a moonless night, the stars are reflected hugely in the still waters of the bay. Dolphins swim past, hunting a midnight snack.

Accessible by boat, canoe, and kayak from Whitewater Bay. Accessible by canoe or kayak only, via Hell’s Bay Canoe Trail (starts off park road).

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. The site can be difficult to get to from Whitewater Bay. A nautical chart is necessary to find the way. This is a manatee habitat. Be cautious! Do not hammer nails or stakes into chickees. Vault toilet. Portable stove only.  

Located:

  • 4.0 miles from Hells Bay Trailhead
  • 2.0 miles from Hells Bay Chickee
  • 1.0 mile from Lard Can campsite
  • 4.5 miles from Lane Bay Chickee

467531413.name: Pearl Bay Chickee (Accessible)

467531414.description:
This site is located in a tiny cove on the Roberts River, which is approximately 100 feet wide and narrows in some places to less than 20 feet. It sits out a bit from the mangrove shoreline behind it. Its western exposure gives campers a lovely view of the sunset. At dinnertime, an alligator may cruise past. Do not encourage him by dumping any food scraps into the water.

Access - Accessible by powerboat, canoe, and kayak. The site can be reached by traveling through Hell’s Bay via major creeks due North, or by boating up the Roberts River from Whitewater Bay.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. The site is accessible from Whitewater Bay by traveling northeast on Robert’s River. There is some tidal influence with an average water depth of approximately 2.5 feet. This is a manatee habitat. Be cautious! Do not hammer nails or stakes into chickees. Vault toilet. Portable stove or grill only.  

Located:

  • 5.5 miles from Coast Guard Marker #30
  • 3.0 miles from North River Chickee
  • 5.5 miles from Lane Bay Chickee
  • 13.5 miles from Flamingo Marina via Whitewater Bay

467531414.name: Robert’s River Chickee

467531415.description:
Located on the south shore of a branch of the Little Shark River, 0.3 miles south of WW marker #6. This is a shady site, with northern exposure. The chickee is tucked up against a tall red mangrove forest. The rattling and plopping and thunkings of the forest residents will be heard all night long.  

Accessible by boat, canoe, and kayak at all tides. Be aware of the strong tidal current and plan your route accordingly. Wilderness Waterway travelers will access the chickee from the Little Shark River. Others may take on the challenge of the aptly named Labyrinth route and approach from the southeast.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. Tidal fluctuations can be as much as 2 to 3 feet. Moor vessels securely! Do not hammer nails or stakes into chickees. Vault toilet. Portable stove or grill only. Pack out all trash. Warning signs advise against eating bass caught in this area due to high mercury content.

Located:

  • 10.0 miles from Harney River
  • 8.5 miles from Canepatch
  • 8.0 miles from Graveyard Creek
  • 5.0 miles from Oyster Bay Chickee

467531415.name: Shark River Chickee

467531416.description:
This campsite is located northwest of Flamingo in a bay off the Joe River. It is a good all day trip from Flamingo if paddlers leave early and the wind and weather are good. The chickee is set far out from the shores of the bay, exposed to bug-banishing breezes from all sides. Fish splash a syncopated beat all night long beneath the chickee.

Access - Accessible by boat, canoe, and kayak at all tides. Located on the Joe River, approximately ½ mile north of Little Fox Lake. Using the Joe River allows boaters to avoid the big waters of Whitewater Bay, although the stretch of Whitewater Bay between Tarpon Creek and the Joe River can get quite rough on windy days.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. This area is manatee habitat. Do not hammer nails or stakes into chickees. Vault toilet. Portable stove or grill only. Pack out all trash. 

Located:

  • 11.5 miles from Whitewater Bay Ramp in Flamingo
  • 6.0 miles from Joe River Chickee
  • 10.0 miles from Oyster Bay Chickee

467531416.name: South Joe River Chickee

467531417.description:
Chickee. This site is located on the northwest corner of a large island surrounded by low mangroves. It is well protected from prevailing winds and rough seas, although it is exposed to the northerly winds which follow cold fronts. It may have mosquitoes during winter days. 

Accessible by boat, canoe, and kayak at all tides. Located off the Wilderness Waterway, 2.5 miles northeast of Coast Guard marker #36 in Whitewater Bay.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. This area is manatee habitat. Do not hammer nails or stakes into chickees. Vault toilet. Portable stove or grill only. Pack out all trash. 

Located:

  • 3.0 miles from North River Chickee
  • 6.0 miles from Roberts River Chickee
  • 8.0 miles from Oyster Bay Chickee
  • 3.0 miles from Coast Guard Marker #34

467531417.name: Watson River Chickee

467531418.description:
Beach Site. This campsite is an open shelly sand beach stretching for several miles along the Gulf of Mexico. Expect expansive sea views as well as magnificent sunsets and sunrises. Ruins of a dock used by an old concession tour may be found here. In the 1830s, Fort Poinsett was located here. Its mission was to thwart suspected arms trading between Indians and Spanish fisherman. Mosquitoes and sandflies may be a problem year round. Raccoons are in the area; store food and water appropriately.

Accessible by powerboat, canoe or kayak via Florida Bay. The Bear Lake Canal is overgrown and impassible and should not be attempted as an alternate route between the Cape beaches and Flamingo.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. The site affords no protection for boats in bad weather. Fires are permitted below the high tide line. Use dead/down wood only. All plants, animals and artifacts in the park are protected, including seashells. Pack out all trash, including toilet paper, and bury human waste 6” deep.  

Located:

  • 10.0 miles from Flamingo Marina (via Florida Bay)
  • 13.5 miles from Bear Lake Trailhead
  • 3.0 miles from Clubhouse Beach
  • 4.5 miles from Middle Cape Sable
  • 5.0 miles from Carl Ross Key

467531418.name: East Cape Sable (Beach Sites)

467531419.description:
This campsite, popular with fishermen, is a long, shelly sand beach on the Gulf of Mexico. There is little shade, and it is exposed to wind in all directions. Campers will find spectacular sunrises and sunsets and unparalleled views of the Gulf or Mexico. Raccoons are in the area; store food and water in appropriately.

Accessible by powerboat, canoe or kayak via Florida Bay and the Gulf of Mexico. The site is exposed; canoes and kayaks should be pulled far onto shore in case the wind picks up. Powerboats should anchor from the bow in unfavorable weather to avoid swamping.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. The site affords no protection for boats in bad weather. Winter storms commonly produce swamped motorboats. Fires are permitted below the high tide line. Use dead/down wood only. All plants, animals and artifacts in the park are protected, including seashells. Pack out all trash, including toilet paper, and bury human waste 6” deep. Portable toilet is recommended.

Located:

  • 14.5 miles from Flamingo Marina (via Florida Bay)
  • 7.5 miles from Clubhouse Beach
  • 4.5 miles from East Cape Sable
  • 5.0 miles from Northwest Cape Sable

467531419.name: Middle Cape Sable (Beach Sites)

467531420.description:
Beach Site. This campsite is an open shelly sand beach with no shade. It is exposed to sun and wind in all directions. Mosquitoes and sandflies may be a present year round. Raccoons are in the area; store food and water in appropriately (hard sided containers). Beautiful sunsets and a sense of wilderness solitude will reward campers here, at this least frequented of the three Cape Sable beaches.

Accessible by powerboat, canoe or kayak via Florida Bay and the Gulf of Mexico. The site is open; canoes and kayaks should be pulled far onto shore in case the wind picks up. Powerboats should anchor from the bow in unfavorable weather to avoid swamping.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. The site affords no protection for boats in bad weather. Winter storms commonly produce swamped motorboats. Fires are permitted below the high tide line. Use dead/down wood only. All plants, animals and artifacts in the park are protected, including seashells. Pack out all trash and bury human waste 6” deep. Portable toilet is recommended.

Located:

  • 11.0 miles from Graveyard Creek
  • 13.0 miles from Oyster Bay Chickee
  • 5.0 miles from Middle Cape Sable
  • 9.5 miles from East Cape Sable

467531420.name: Northwest Cape Sable (Beach Sites)

467531421.description:
Ground Site. One of only 2 Keys open to camping in Florida Bay. Popular with fishermen. With buddy and dive flag, one can snorkel in the moat area. There is an open grassy area for camping. Mangrove trees provide shelter from sun and wind.  

Accessible to powerboats approaching cautiously via the marked channel from the southeast to the moat near the key, at all tides. Paddlers, be wary of the long open water crossings. Public boat ramps are in Flamingo and the Upper Keys; none at the Key Largo Ranger Station.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. For conditions and closures please call the Flamingo VC.

All keys and beaches in Florida Bay are closed to landing unless otherwise designated. Crocodile Sanctuary is closed to all public entry. No ground fires allowed. Use camp stove only. Dock, vault toilet, picnic tables. All plants, animals and artifacts in the park are protected, including seashells.  

Located:

  • 11.0 miles from Flamingo Marina
  • 20.0 miles from Upper Florida Keys public/private Ramps
  • 20.0 miles from North Nest Key

467531421.name: Little Rabbit Key (Ground Sites)

467531422.description:
Ground Site. One of only 2 Keys open to camping in Florida Bay. This site is popular with boaters and can be very busy area, especially on weekends. Snorkelers should be cautious: use a dive flag with a buddy. And be alert for other boats in the area.

Accessible to powerboats at all tides. Not recommended for paddlers due to long distance over open water, unless launching from Key Largo. The dock will accommodate several vessels. Located 5 miles west of Upper Florida Keys.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. For conditions and closures please call the Flamingo VC. 

All Keys (islands) and beaches in Florida Bay are closed to landing unless otherwise designated. Crocodile Sanctuary is closed to all public entry. No ground fires allowed. Use camp stove only. Dock, vault toilet, picnic tables. All plants, animals and artifacts in the park are protected, including seashells. Pack out all trash.

Located:

  • 8.0 miles from launch points in upper Keys
  • 20.0 miles from Little Rabbit Key
  • 23.0 miles from Flamingo Marina

467531422.name: North Nest Key (Ground Sites)

467531423.description:
This is a double Chickee on Florida Bay 6 miles south of Flamingo, next to Johnson Key. It is exposed to wind and waves from all sides. It is elevated considerably above the water compared to other chickees. 

Access from Flamingo is via the marked channel on the west side of Murray Key and Clive Key. Access from the south is via Man of War Channel.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. This chickee is elevated above the water higher than most chickees. A loading dock facilitates access to the platforms. Approach is in moderately shallow water.  

Motor boats must be careful not to damage the sea grass near chickee. Canoes and kayaks should use care in the channels at low tide to give power boats room to pass.

Located:

  • 7 miles south of the Flamingo Marina via the Clive Key Channel
  • 10 miles from Shark Point Chickee
  • 11.4 miles from Little Rabbit Key

467531423.name: Johnson Key Chickee

467531424.description:
This is a double chickee located out in the open water of Florida Bay. It is fairly exposed on all sides. The approach to the chickee is in shallow water and may be difficult at lower tides. 

From Flamingo Marina take Tin Can Channel east to Buoy Key and Shark Point. From the east follow nautical chart.

description_map.need_to_know:
If you are departing from Key Largo or Flamingo you do NOT need to pick up your printed wilderness permit in the park. Proof of digital reservations / permits or printouts are allowed for the Flamingo and Key Largo areas. Motor boats must be careful not to damage sea grass. Canoes and kayaks should use care in the channels at low tide to give power boats room to pass. This chickee is elevated above the water higher than most chickees. A loading dock facilitates access to the tent platforms. Approach is in moderately shallow water. 

Located: 

  • 8.5 miles east of Flamingo via Tin Can Channel
  • 10 miles from Johnson Key Chickee

467531424.name: Shark Point Chickee

467531425.description:
Ground site. Located on the south bank of the Broad River near WW marker #25. This site can get muddy after a heavy rain and mosquitoes can be prolific due to the dense mangroves nearby. Facilities are located on a small clearing of high ground surrounded by tall trees. This wide river eventually flows into Rodger’s River. It is reported that Joe Wiggins had a floating store on Broad River early in the century.                                                          

Accessible to both canoes/kayaks and powerboats at all tides. Note the “Nightmare” section of the Wilderness Waterway must be navigated on a high tide – it is too shallow otherwise even for canoes/kayaks. The coastal route should be taken during low or falling tides.

description_map.need_to_know:
Be prepared for strong river currents and up to a 3ft tidal differential when mooring your vessel at this campsite. No ground fires permitted. Portable grills/stoves only. Small dock, canoe/kayak ramp, vault toilet, picnic tables 

Located:

  • 8.0 miles from South Lostmans 
  • 4.0 miles from Highland Beach 
  • 9.5 miles from Camp Lonesome
  • 8.5 miles from Harney River

467531425.name: Broad River (Ground Sites)

467531426.description:
Ground site. Located on an old Calusa Indian mound and shaded by tropical hardwood trees. The Seminole Indians had a hunting camp here when the Park was established in 1947. At least one Seminole claimed to have grown up at his family’s home at Camp Lonesome. This site is one of the few which extends inland into the sawgrass prairie. Paddlers may want to explore the Wood River (unmarked) just south of the site.

Accessible to both canoes/kayaks and powerboats at all tides. Located 3 miles off the Wilderness Waterway by traveling from marker #26 in Broad River Bay up the Broad River. At the large fork in the river, look for a small dock on the north river bank partly obscured by vegetation to find the campsite.

description_map.need_to_know:
Warning signs advise against eating bass caught in this area due to high mercury content. Plants, animals and artifacts in the park are protected. No ground fires permitted. Portable grills/stoves only. Small dock, vault toilet, picnic tables 

Located:

  • 10.5 miles from Willy Willy 
  • 7.0 miles from Rodger’s River 
  • 9.5 miles from Broad River

467531426.name: Camp Lonesome (Ground Sites)

467531427.description: GROUND SITE. This flat clearing was a homestead built from shell and cement by Arthur Darwin, who lived there from 1945 to 1971. He was the last private resident on Park lands. Artifacts from the site can still be seen and are protected. Tie your vessel securely. The island is also known as Opossum Key named because of the great number of opossums killed on the island. Before this, it was known as Chevelier Place, named after Jean Chevelier, a plume hunter who lived here. There is no dock and the WW is used frequently by passing boaters.

description_map.need_to_know: The Gopher Creek / Charley Creek (Gulf of Mexico to Darwins Place campsite) route is not passable. It is blocked by trees on the Gulf side. Accessible to both canoes/kayaks and powerboats at all tides. Located between Chevelier Bay and Cannon Bay on the Wilderness Waterway between markers #86 and #87. Note: older nautical charts call Darwin’s Place “Opossum Key.”

467531427.name: Darwin’s Place (Ground Sites)

467531428.description:
Beach site. Located between Highland Point and the beaches north of the mouth of Rodger’s River. There are many large coconut palms growing along this narrow beach and it is a good location for bird watching. Make sure your camp is set up above the high tide line and secure food from racoons. The Rewis family lived at this site for about 27 years and spent most of it on the beach. Australian Pines, exotics to the area, can still be seen today. 

Access for canoes/kayaks and powerboats is limited due to exposed mud flats near the shoreline at low tide. Boaters should also consider the level of exposure to strong westerly winds at this site during bad weather which can make travel very difficult.

description_map.need_to_know:
Make sure your vessels are tied, beached or anchored securely. Use dead/downed wood below storm surge line. No facilities. Pack out all trash and bury human waste 6”.  

Located:

  • 4.0 miles from Broad River 
  • 12.5 miles from Harney River 
  • 9.0 miles from Graveyard Creek

467531428.name: Highland Beach (Beach Sites)

467531429.description: Beach site. Excellent fishing areas are only minutes away to both the north and the south. Paddlers may choose to use Hog Key to shorten days between Lostman’s River and Turkey Key due to traditionally rougher seas in that area. Access may be difficult and should be done at a higher tide. Access for canoes/kayaks and powerboats is limited due to exposed mud flats near the shoreline at low tide. Be prepared to anchor away from shore and wade into the site. Recommended for canoes and kayaks only.

description_map.need_to_know:
Be prepared for strong winds and rough seas when anchoring a powerboat. Two anchors are strongly recommended for this site. Use dead/downed wood below storm surge line. No facilities. Pack out all trash and bury human waste 6”. 

Located:

  • 5.5 miles from Turkey Key  
  • 11.0 miles from Broad River 
  • 7.0 miles from Highland Beach

467531429.name: Hog Key (Beach Sites)

467531430.description:
Beach site. This beach site is located on a small key in the Ten Thousand Islands. The camping area is located on a sandy spit near the outhouse. Proper food storage is important as there are a number of resident raccoons on this island. 

Accessible by powerboat, kayak, and canoe. There is deep water access from the direction of Sandfly Pass. A sandbar has filled in the passage between Jewell Key and its neighbor to the north.

description_map.need_to_know:
Nautical charts and GPS are helpful in locating this small island. Once you find this lovely sandy spit, you will not be alone. Store your food and water in hard-sided containers to foil the resident rodent population. Pack out all trash, including food scraps. All plants, animals, and artifacts in the Park are protected, including seashells. Use dead/downed wood below storm surge line. No facilities. Pack out all trash and bury human waste 6”. 

Located:

  • 5.5 miles from Everglades City  
  • 3.5 miles from Rabbit Key 
  • 5.0 miles from Picnic Key 
  • 7.1 miles from Pavilion Key

467531430.name: Jewell Key (Beach Sites)

467531431.description:
Ground site. Closest campsite on the Wilderness Waterway to Everglades City, located between marker #126 and #127 on the southern bank of the Lopez River. This campsite is easily located by spotting the cement cistern which marks the old Lopez homestead built at the turn of the century. 

Accessible to both canoes/kayaks and powerboats at all tides. Caution: Moor your vessel carefully! There is no dock and other vessels pass by closely to avoid oyster bars in the river.

description_map.need_to_know:
Lopez River is well traveled by powerboats due to its closeness to civilization. Mosquitoes can be heavy both early and late in the winter season. The old cistern is the site’s most visible feature from the river. The Lopez family lived here for 2 generations. One of the only weddings remembered by locals at that time took place here between Walter Alderman and Marie Lopez. No ground fires permitted. Portable grills/stoves only. Vault toilet, picnic tables. 

Located:

  • 8.0 miles from Everglades City  
  • 10.0 miles from Pavilion Key 
  • 11.5 miles from Sweetwater Chickee

467531431.name: Lopez River (Ground Sites)

467531432.description:
Ground site. Located on a clearing of higher ground with a few palm trees that provide shade. This site was once an inholding. Soil compaction at this site can cause flooding during rainy weather. The dock is larger than most and can accommodate several vessels. This is a popular site for fishing groups with powerboats. 

Accessible to both canoes/kayaks and powerboats at all tides. May not be marked on older nautical charts. Located just east of the Wilderness Waterway at the mouth of Lostman’s Five Creek, between marker #60 and #62.

description_map.need_to_know:
Feeding alligators is prohibited! Alligators are common at this site and have been known to lose their fear of people when fed. No ground fires permitted. Portable grills/stoves only. Large dock, vault toilet, picnic tables. 

Located:

  • 1.0 mile from Plate Creek  
  • 6.5 miles from Darwin’s Place 
  • 10.5 miles from Willy Willy

467531432.name: Lostman’s Five (Ground Sites)

467531433.description:
Beach site. There is good fishing in the area located near the mouth of the Huston and Chatham Rivers. Make sure your camp is set up above the high tide line. Make sure vessels are tied, beached, or anchored securely. 

Accessible to canoes/kayaks at all tides, and powerboats most of the time if approached cautiously. The best site is located on the West end of the Key facing Chatham Bend. This key is exposed to W-NW winds in stormy weather.

description_map.need_to_know:
Richard Hamilton and his family lived here in 1895. It is called Mormon Key because Richard allegedly had 2 living wives, though he only lived with one. Use dead/downed wood below storm surge line. No facilities. Pack out all trash and bury human waste 6”. 

Located:

  • 4.5 miles from Pavilion Key  
  • 4.0 miles from Watson’s Place 
  • 2.0 miles from New Turkey Key 
  • 3.0 miles from Turkey Key

467531433.name: Mormon Key (Beach Sites)

467531434.description:
Beach site. The site in the middle of the key has a vault toilet nearby, but is buggy. The other site is on an open sand spit which usually has less bugs, but at high tide you must use a boat to reach the toilet in the middle of the key. The sand spit is getting smaller with time. 

Accessible to canoes/kayaks and powerboats at all tides. To reach the camping areas stay in the deep-water channel to the east of the piles. There are two different camping areas, one at the north end of the key and the other is in the middle.

description_map.need_to_know:
New Turkey Key is often confused by nearby Turkey Key. There is camping on the spit at the north end. This was once a central location for trout fishing activities. Ice boats once made fish pick-ups here and some of the pilings still remain. Use dead/downed wood below storm surge line. Vault toilet.

Located:

  • 6.5 miles from Pavilion Key  
  • 6.0 miles from Watson’s Place 
  • 2.0 miles from Mormon Key 
  • 1.0 miles from Turkey Key

467531434.name: New Turkey Key (Beach Sites)

467531435.description:
Beach site. Choose a site away from vegetation to minimize the impact on this fragile area. Bird watching is popular on the shoreline and fishing in the area is good. Tie or anchor your vessel securely and protect your food from raccoons.

Accessible to canoes/kayaks and powerboats at all tides. Campsite is at the northern end of the Key only, south of the porta-john is closed to all landing and access. There is protected anchorage offshore of the campsite area under most wind conditions.

description_map.need_to_know:
Camping is permitted on the north side of the key only! Use dead/downed wood below storm surge line. Vault toilet.

Located:

  • 13.0 miles from Everglades City
  • 10.5 miles from Indian Key
  • 10.0 miles from Lopez River 
  • 8.0 miles from Watson’s Place
  • 4.5 miles from Mormon Key
  • 6.5 miles from New Turkey Key

467531435.name: Pavilion Key (Beach Sites)

467531436.description:
Beach site. Campsites are located along the narrow beach. The channel offshore of the site is deep and swift with numerous oyster bars on the bottom. This site can be very buggy when calm and is exposed to westerly winds in stormy weather. Camp well above the high tide line.

Accessible to canoes/kayaks and powerboats at all tides at campsite area on the SW side of Picnic Key just east of the small mangrove island in the channel between Picnic and Tiger Keys. Only the north end of the beach has water deep enough for powerboats. Other potential sites are inaccessible at low tide. Make sure vessels are tied, beached, or anchored securely.

description_map.need_to_know:
In years gone by, people used to come to Picnic Key for their big picnic dinners. Use dead/downed wood below storm surge line. Vault toilet.

Located:

  • 8.0 miles from Everglades City
  • 1.0 miles from Tiger Key 
  • 12.0 miles from Pavilion Key

467531436.name: Picnic Key (Beach Sites)

467531437.description:
Beach site. This site is located at the mouth of Rabbit Key Pass on the eastern side of the island. A vault toilet marks the designated site. This campsite is a narrow beach with dune vegetation. Be aware of prickly pear cactus near toilet. 

Accessible to canoes/kayaks and powerboats by approaching from the south either between Crate Key and Rabbit Key or around the back of Crate Key. Easily accessible from Rabbit Key Pass.

description_map.need_to_know:
This site can be used in a short 2-night loop trip. A sand spit bridges the two islands – at low tides boats may become stranded. The sandbar on the right is not recommended for camping because of flooding at high tide. The infamous Ed Watson was buried there, then later his son-in-law came and reburied his body in Ft. Myers. Use dead/downed wood below storm surge line. Portable stove/grill recommended. Vault toilet. 

Located:

  • 6.0 miles from Chokoloskee Island 
  • 6.0 miles from Indian Key  
  • 4.0 miles from Pavilion Key 
  • 9.0 miles from Everglades City

467531437.name: Rabbit Key (Beach Sites)

467531438.description:
Beach site. The sites on the western side offer a nice breeze and more privacy. Locate your campsite away from vegetation to minimize your impact in this fragile area. 

Camp along the western shoreline, but be aware of shallow water and limited access at low tides. Make sure your vessels are tied, beached, or anchored securely.

description_map.need_to_know:
There is deep water around the northern side. On the west side is a quiet, secluded beach only accessible by canoe/kayak due to the shallow waters. Use dead/downed wood below storm surge line. No facilities. Pack out all trash and bury human waste 6”. Vault toilet on nearby Picnic Key.

Located:

  • 1.0 mile from Picnic Key 
  • 3.0 miles from Indian Key
  • 9.0 miles from Everglades City

467531438.name: Tiger Key (Beach Sites)

467531439.description:
Beach site. The beach is narrow and sloping in many places, but a few flat spots can be found. Watch out for prickly pear cactus and protect fragile vegetation.

Accessible to canoes/kayaks and small powerboats with shallow draft at all tides, but some areas are mucky near the shore at low tide. The site most frequently used is at the SE end, but beach areas are also found in the middle of the west side too.

description_map.need_to_know:
The Gopher Creek / Charley Creek route is not passable. It is blocked by trees on the Gulf side. At high tide a small vessel with shallow draft can explore Pelican Bay for good fishing and birdwatching – with local knowledge and charts. This key was used often by fishermen who lived in shacks until Hurricane Donna. Many then moved onto houseboats and had run boats bring supplies and take away their catch. When the run boat service ceased, so did living on the key. Use dead/downed wood below storm surge line. No facilities. Pack out all trash and bury human waste 6”. 

Located:

  • 7.0 mile from Pavilion Key  
  • 7.0 miles from Watson’s Place 
  • 3.0 miles from Mormon Key 
  • 1.0 mile from New Turkey Key

467531439.name: Turkey Key (Beach Sites)

467531440.description:
Ground site. At the turn of the century Ed Watson lived here in a two-story house growing vegetables and refining sugarcane. Historic objects can still be located including: a cement cistern, a sugarcane syrup cauldron, and farm machinery. Several exotic plant species still grow at this site.

Accessible to both canoes/kayaks and powerboats at all tides. Located by leaving the Wilderness Waterway at marker #100 and heading 1 1/2 miles down the Chatham River. There is a sign on the dock marking the campsite located on the north side of the river.

description_map.need_to_know:
If prepared for mosquitoes, this is a good area to explore by foot. Remember, all plants, animals, and artifacts in the park are protected. This site is named after Ed Watson who lived here until 1910. Watson was suspected of several murders. Shortly after the body of Hannah Smith was found floating nearby in the Chatham River, Watson was gunned down by frightened townsmen in Chokoloskee. No ground fires permitted. Portable grills/stoves only. Long dock, canoe ramp, vault toilet, picnic tables. 

Located:

  • 3.5 miles from Sweetwater Chickee 
  • 4.5 miles from Darwin’s Place 
  • 8.0 miles from Pavilion Key 
  • 4.0 miles from Mormon Key

467531440.name: Watson’s Place (Ground Sites)

467531441.description:
Ground site. This campsite is located on an old Calusa Indian mound, shaded by tropical hardwood trees. A canoe can follow the narrow, winding creek that connects the west end of Rocky Creek Bay to Lostman’s Five Bay to explore a different route back to the Wilderness Waterway.

Accessible to both canoes/kayaks and powerboats at all tides. Site is 2 miles off the Wilderness Waterway east of marker #39 then north up Rocky Creek (watch for rocks). Bear left in Rocky Creek Bay to reach the campsite (the map incorrectly shows site to the right).

description_map.need_to_know:
All plants, animals, and artifacts in the park are protected. The Calusa Indian mounds were made from the remains of shellfish. They built the higher ground on which they lived to get away from the mosquitoes and flood waters. No ground fires permitted. Portable grills/stoves only. Small dock, vault toilet, picnic tables. 

Located:

  • 10.5 miles from Camp Lonesome 
  • 10.5 miles from Lostman’s Five 
  • 5.5 miles from Rodgers River Chickee

467531441.name: Willy Willy (Ground Sites)

467531442.description:
Double Chickee. At marker #126, look for the “No Wake” sign – this marks the entrance to the passage where the chickee is located. Listen for dolphins at night. Curious sea turtles may surface from time to time. The chickee is sheltered from all but the strongest breezes. Mosquitoes may visit in the early morning and evening hours. 

Accessible to both canoes/kayaks and powerboats at all tides.

description_map.need_to_know:
Many nautical charts and guidebooks have not been updated and still list the obsolete Sunday Bay chickee. Be aware of the correct chickee location at marker 126. The walkway connecting this chickee’s platform is shorter than most. As a result, there is not enough space between the platforms to safely cross-moor a 17-ft boat. Be prepared to moor your boat against the back of the platform. When securing your boat afloat, be aware of the reversing tidal current and the 3-ft tide differential. Portable stove or grill only. Dock, vault toilet. 

Located:

  • 9.0 miles from Everglades City 
  • 6.0 miles from Chokoloskee 
  • 1.0 mile from Lopez River 
  • 10.5 miles from Sweetwater Chickee

467531442.name: Crooked Creek Chickee

467531443.description:
Chickee. Located on a small key facing SE. This key gets good air circulation, making it more insect free than most. Free standing tents are needed for chickee sites. Do not hammer stakes or nails into chickee. 

Accessible to canoes/kayaks and powerboats (up to 21 feet) at all tides. Located on the Key SW of the WW between marker #65 and #63 in Plate Creek Bay. No wake zones in Plate and Alligator Creeks. Overhanging branches may obstruct vessels with T-tops or sailboats with fixed masts.

description_map.need_to_know:
This large-sized chickee was built before the park was established and was originally used as a base camp for Joseph Cotton’s real estate sales and his hunting/fishing parties. Portable stove or grill only. Long dock, vault toilet. 

Located:

  • 10.0 miles from Watson’s Place 
  • 10.5 miles from Sweetwater Chickee  
  • 5.5 miles from Darwin’s Place

467531443.name: Plate Creek Chickee

467531444.description:
Double Chickee. This chickee is set in the middle of a small protected cove. It is far enough from the mangroves and situated so that it usually gets a breeze off the water and has few mosquitoes. The nearby bays offer good tarpon fishing and there is access to freshwater bass fishing as well. Eating bass caught in this area is not advised due to high mercury content. 

Accessible to canoes/kayaks and powerboats at all tides. Located by traveling SW along the shoreline from W.W. marker #32 about 3/4 of a mile. If traveling to this site from the North, copy the W.W. re-route from marker #39 to #35 onto your chart. Free standing tents are needed – do not hammer stakes or nails into chickee.

description_map.need_to_know:
Three families lived in Rodgers River around thee 1900’s. Livingston Atwell, his father Shelton Atwell, and Mr. Evans and family. Atwell grew sugar cane and vegetables. Alligators and deer were said to be plentiful. The Atwells left after 25 years to move to Key West. Portable stove or grill only. Long dock, vault toilet. 

Located:

  • 10.5 miles from Broad River 
  • 5.5 miles from Willy Willy  
  • 5.5 miles from Camp Lonesome

467531444.name: Rodger’s River Chickee

467531445.description:
Double Chickee. Sweetwater is located in a less frequently traveled area. Bring a free-standing tent with extra rope to tie it down. No hammering stakes or nails into chickee. 

Accessible to canoes/kayaks at all tides. Powerboats should have a shallow draft, low profile, and be 18 feet or less in length. This site is 1 1/2 miles off of the marked Wilderness Waterway route, on the north end of a small island on Sweetwater Creek. From marker #102 head toward compass bearing 120 degrees then head north on Sweetwater Creek. From marker #97 or #99, head NE to Sweetwater Creek then north.

description_map.need_to_know:
“Sweetwater” is a local term for fresh water, which accurately describes this site’s location near the transition between brackish and fresh water. Portable stove or grill only. Long dock, vault toilet. 

Located:

  • 11.5 miles from Lopez River 
  • 3.5 miles from Watson’s Place  
  • 5.0 miles from Darwin’s Place

467531445.name: Sweetwater Chickee

467531447.description:
Ground Site. Trailside grassy area that backs up to a cypress forest to the north, perfect for exploration. Camp alongside the Old Ingraham Highway, the first road leading to Flamingo, completed in the early 1920’s. Opportunity to see alligators, turtles, and a variety of birds in freshwater marsh and cypress habitats. 

Access - Accessible on foot or horseback along the Old Ingraham Highway Hiking Trail. From the Main Park Road, turn onto the road towards Royal Palm. Take the first right towards Hidden Lake, then continue straight for 1.5 miles until you reach the Old Ingraham Highway trailhead. Campsite is located along the northern trailside as the trail bends westward.

Max people = 8

Max Group = 1

Max nights per trip = 3

description_map.need_to_know:
Your reservation confirmation email will serve as your permit. You are NOT required to pick up a physical permit in person, but you must carry a physical copy or screenshot of your permit. No facilities provided. Portable toilet is recommended. All plants, animals and artifacts in the park are protected. Absolutely no ground fires allowed! All cooking and heating must be accomplished with devices that will not produce a spark or ember that is capable of igniting vegetation. Wood, charcoal, or coal fueled grills or stoves are not permitted. Leave no trace principals must be used. Pack out all trash.

Located:

3.5 miles from Old Ingraham Highway trailhead

6.4 miles from Ingraham campsite

Approximate Coordinates:

80°39'13.40"W

467531447.name: Ernest Coe (Ground Sites)

467531448.description:
Ground Site. Grassy area at the terminus of the Old Ingraham Highway Trail. Camp alongside the Old Ingraham Highway, the first road leading to Flamingo, completed in the early 1920’s. Opportunity to see alligators, turtles, and a variety of birds in freshwater marsh and cypress habitats.

Access - Accessible on foot or horseback along the Old Ingraham Highway Hiking Trail. From the Main Park Road, turn onto the road to Royal Palm. Take the first right towards Hidden Lake, then continue straight for 1.5 miles until you reach the Old Ingraham Highway trailhead. Campsite is located at the end of the trail.
